Samira / Jordan —

Thanks for the data, Samira. I sketched a concise sensitivity and fallback recommendation attached (summary pasted below). I focused on three SKU pillars: H100 (memory+perf), A100 (balanced), and L4 (cost-efficient inference).

Executive summary (short):
- Recommendation: Reserve a mixed pool: 30% H100, 50% A100, 20% L4.
  - Rationale: H100 nodes absorb long-context (~16k) research route without forced offloading; A100 provides steady gen throughput and higher concurrency; L4 serves batch embeddings and non-critical chat fallback to minimize cost.

Sensitivity snapshot (high level):
- Long-context research route (16k seq): requires ~80 GB usable GPU memory per concurrent request to avoid heavy KV offload; H100 (80GB) can handle ~4 concurrent long-context slots per device at target latency. A100 (40GB) will need more aggressive tiling/eviction and will hit 99th pct latency risks above ~2 concurrent long-context slots. L4 (24 GB) not recommended for native long-context without sharding.
- Real-time generation (avg 512 tokens): latency sensitivity mostly driven by compute; L4 is viable for <=150 qps per device with quantized weights but will push 99th pct beyond 120ms at sustained 350 qps. A100 handles 350 qps with moderate batching; H100 gives headroom for burst to 700 qps with our dynamic tiling.

Fallback and routing policy (ops-friendly):
- Primary routing: priority routes -> pinned model variants on H100/A100 depending on route.
- Degradation path under contention:
  1) Route-level throttling (reduce non-priority requests)
  2) Auto-fallback to quantized A100/L4 variant for non-realtime routes (embeddings, background inference)
  3) For gen route bursts, fallback to A100-quantized then L4-quantized with explicit latency & quality regression monitoring and automated rollback after 30 min if regressions > 5%

Cost/commit framing:
- Proposed reserve: commit to 40 A100-equivalent units (convertible across SKUs) for Q4; allow up to 30% burstable pool billed hourly. We can map 1 H100 = 2.0 A100-equivalents; 1 L4 = 0.35 A100-equivalents for econ conversions.

Operational notes (Ben, feel free to add):
- KV cache hit-rate is critical for long-context economics; recommend pre-warming common prefixes and instrumenting telemetry for eviction rates.
- Autoscaling buffer: keep 10% spare GPU slots during business hours to avoid hitting fallbacks during predictable bursts.

Next steps: Jordan will capture these in a short mutual action plan and share the procurement-friendly tiered pricing. Samira, if that reserve mapping looks sensible, we can draft a 12-month commit + burst appendix.

Best — Irene

Adding a couple of engineering clarifications to Irene's excellent summary: 

- Tiling and KV cache: For 16k contexts we recommend a split strategy: keep active window (last 2k-4k tokens) in GPU KV and offload older context to fast NVMe + async prefetch. H100's larger on-device memory reduces NVMe pressure and avoids tail latency spikes.
- Quantization tolerances: L4 performs well with 4-bit quantization for embeddings and short-context chat. For generation quality-sensitive routes we recommend 8-bit quantized A100 variants as first fallback, only push to 4-bit on L4 if monitoring confirms acceptable degradation.
- Runtime tweaks: enable adaptive batching with dynamic max tokens per batch (cap at 1.5x median tokens) to preserve 99th pct latency during bursts.

I'll coordinate with ops to add telemetry hooks for eviction rate, NVMe I/O latency, and fallback-trigger counts.
